g.text: through research, prototyping and a close
reading of how people use things.
Each project moves from context to a resolved outcome through five clear stages. The route
changes with the problem; the rigor does not.
Understand people, use, market, material and constraints before shaping form.
Keep asking until the problem becomes specific enough to act on.
Use physical and digital trials to reveal what presentation alone cannot.
Compare evidence, identify gaps and refine the architecture.
Bring function, detail, finish and communication into one coherent outcome.
From articulated metal and carved timber to connected electronics and medical-product research—
each project is presented with its full process and evidence.

A low-distraction navigation device that presents only essential
information so riders stay present on the road.
Public furniture shaped around comfort, openness and durability
across changing environments and everyday use.
A compact system for safer moisture removal, better hearing-aid
longevity and a simpler everyday care routine.
